messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles UTC offset | Berlin UTC offset | Time difference (Berlin – LA) |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| **Early March** (before LA’s 2nd Sunday) | UTC‑8 (PST) | UTC+1 (CET) | **9 h** |
| **Late March** (after LA’s 2nd Sunday, before Berlin’s last Sunday) | UTC‑7 (PDT) | UTC+1 (CET) | **8 h** |
| **Late March – Early November** (both on DST) | UTC‑7 (PDT) | UTC+2 (CEST) | **9 h** |
| **Early November – Late October** (after Berlin’s DST ends, before LA’s) | UTC‑7 (PDT) | UTC+1 (CET) | **8 h** |
| **After LA’s DST ends (first Sunday November)** | UTC‑8 (PST) | UTC+0 (GMT) | **8 h** |

### Bottom line
- **Most of the year** (when both cities are on the same DST status) Berlin is **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.
- **During the transition windows** (late March and late October/early November) the difference drops to **8 hours** because the two regions switch daylight‑saving time on different dates.

So, depending on the time of year, you should plan for either an 8‑hour or a 9‑hour time difference.
